problems.question: Evaluate $5^{-2}$ and express your answer as a fraction.
Simplify $\frac{6^4 \times 6^{-2}}{6^3}$, leaving your answer in the form $6^n$.
Calculate $(3 \times 10^4) \times (4 \times 10^{-2})$, giving your answer in standard form.
Simplify $\frac{8^{\frac{2}{3}} \times 4^{-1}}{16^{\frac{1}{2}}}$, expressing your answer in the form $2^n$.

The mass of the Earth is approximately $5.97 \times 10^{24}$ kg and the mass of the Moon is approximately $7.35 \times 10^{22}$ kg. How many times more massive is the Earth than the Moon? Give your answer in standard form to $2$ significant figures.
problems.answer: $$\frac{5.97 \times 10^{24}}{7.35 \times 10^{22}} = \frac{5.97}{7.35} \times 10^{24-22} = 0.8122448 \times 10^2 = 81.22448$$ To $2$ s.f.: $81$. In standard form: $8.1 \times 10^1$. The Earth is about $81$ times more massive than the Moon.
